newsitem.title: USA: Panetta says eyeing economic package for D.C..
newsitem.headline: Panetta says eyeing economic package for D.C..

text.p: White House Chief of Staff Leon Panetta said on Thursday he supports developing an economic package aimed at assisting the District of Columbia, but reiterated that a flat tax is not the answer.

"I've talked to the President about try(ing) to develop, if we can, a package that is targeted to the District of Columbia in a way that ensures that investment will take place within the (city)," Panetta said, in a luncheon speech before a women's political group.
One avenue would be to make the District an "empowerment zone," Panetta said, referring to designations that would ease restrictions on the use of tax exempt bonds for private development.
But he said a workable plan is not to going to happen "overnight."
"It's going to be an effort that everybody has to work together on," Panetta said.
Panetta said he has major concerns with pending bills on Capitol Hill to enact a 15 percent flat tax for D.C. residents and businesses.
"I don't believe Congress can deliver on that promise," Panetta said. "The last thing they need to do to the citizens of the District is promise something they can't deliver."

He added, "I'm not sure that simply cutting rates will, in fact, ensure that that investment will flow back into the District of Columbia. It could be abused in ways that would not assist the city," he said.

Panetta said the administration is committed to working with city officials and D.C.'s delegate to Congress Eleanor Holmes Norton to "develop the kind of package that will (make) D.C. the kind of capital this country deserves. It's something we have to be committed to."
